To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the condensation of calf-thymus DNA is observed in the presence of specific cationic surfactants.
the spacer length, the presence of a specific functional group and the covalently linked headgroups play a crucial role in the DNA condensation process.
The condensation of DNA into the cholesteric-like psi-phase was induced by specific cationic surfactants with different stereochemistry and spacer lengths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the spacer in the condensation and the formation of DNA-lipid aggregates.
the effect of the gemini amphiphile spacer in the condensation and the morphology of DNA.
the role of the spacer of the cationic geminis in the condensation process of DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the condensation of calf-thymus DNA into a cholesteric phase is a consequence of the presence of specific cationic amphiphiles with a gemini structure.
the spacer of gemini surfactant plays a crucial role in the condensation process.
the spacer length of cationic surfactants is an important factor in the DNA condensation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gemini surfactant condensation of DNA is highly dependent on the spacer length, and that the presence of a covalent link in the spacer is a key feature in this process.
the spacer of cations amphiphiles plays an important role in the condensation and stabilization of DNA.
the spacer of the gemini amphiphile is a crucial factor in the condensation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of specific groups, such as the hydroxypropyl group, in the spacer of the gemini surfactant, and the coexistence of a spacer with two different stereochemistries, can lead to a more efficient condensation of DNA, as well as to a higher DNA loading.
a chiral spacer in a gemini surfactant can induce the formation of a cholesteric phase in the presence of DNA.
the condensing ability of gemini amphiphilic surfactants is related to the spacer length and the presence of specific headgroups.
